sentences.text:
By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
217 of 2023 at Police Station- Mugalsarai, District- Chandauli under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 5j(ii)/6 of the POCSO Act.
The applicant is in jail since 15.08.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 26.10.2023.

The following arguments made by Sri Ashutosh Kumar Pandey, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Sri Chandan Agarwal, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 16 years in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2. The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.
55026 of 2021) is contested on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.

entities.text:
Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.
55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no lawful basis for the age related entry in the school record.
The school records disclosing her age as 16 years and 6 months are unreliable.
(iii) The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has asserted that she is 17 years of age.

(iv) No medical examination to determine the correct age of the victim as per the latest scientific criteria and medical protocol by eminent doctors from a reputed institution was got done by the prosecution as the same would have established the majority of the victim and falsified the prosecution case.
The victim is in fact a major.
3. The victim and the applicant were intimate and had consensual physical relations.
4. The FIR is a result of the said relationship going awry.
5. The applicant never gave a plighted word to marry the victim.
6. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship with the applicant.

sentences.text: 7. The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has stated that she accompanied the applicant to Arya Samaj Mandir of her own volition.
The victim has further asserted that she entered into a consensual physical relations on account of promise to marry.
8. The statement of the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is significantly different from the one under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
According to the said statement the victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that the applicant blackmailed the victim into having physical relations with him.
9. The applicant did not capture any indecent photographs or videos of the victim and none were recovered from him.
10. The victim in her statement before the doctor has asserted that she has solemnized her marriage with the applicant and she is an expectant mother.
11. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
The conduct of the victim shows that she was a consenting party.
12. Medical evidence to establish the commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
13. Major inconsistencies in the statements of the victim under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C. as well as the recitals in the F.I.R. discredit the prosecution case.
14. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
15. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Satyam Gond @ Sunil Gond be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

(iii) The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru.
Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. (Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
